title: "What a year of lending tools taught a small community library"

# What a year of lending tools taught a small community library

Northbank Tool Library opened on 1 March 2025 in a shed behind the community hall. Twelve
months later it had 214 members and 380 tools on the shelves, almost all of them donated.

## Who borrowed what

Members took out 1,146 loans in the first year, which works out to about five loans per member.

The volunteer coordinator, Sam Okafor, put it plainly in the annual report: "We've had more drills borrowed than any
other tool, by a long way."

Not everything came home. Nine tools were never returned, and the library's committee wrote them off in February
2026. That's a loss rate I'd guess most lenders would envy.

## Paying for it

A $3,200 grant from the local council covered public liability insurance and the booking software for the first
year. Members pay nothing to join.

## What a booking system can do

ExampleLend is one example of an online lending platform. It sends each borrower a reminder email two days before a
loan is due. As of October 2026, its free plan doesn't send text messages.

If you run something similar, I'd use a reminder like this from day one. In my view it does more for returns than any
late fee would.

## What comes next

The second year starts with a waiting list for the pressure washer and a plan to open on Wednesday evenings as well
as Saturdays.

As I see it, none of this needed a big budget. It needed a shed, a booking system that nags people politely, and a handful of
volunteers who don't mind talking about drills.
